title: Prefill-Decoder Workflow Benchmarking Harness, Regression Anchors, and CI Regression Guards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a focused benchmarking harness that exercises the prefill->decode scheduler intersection with attention-kernel selection in order to produce stable regression anchors for CI perf gates. This ticket covers designing the anchor shard selection strategy, implementing deterministic sequence-phase samplers, integrating noise modeling for quantile thresholds, and wiring CI checks that fail with reproducible diagnostics and suggested remediation actions.
background: Motivation: intermittent regressions in tail latency after kernel-routing changes are hard to triage because current benchmarks mix multiple phases and rarely surface decode-prefill interaction effects.

Existing artifacts: several mixbench and golden-suite tickets exist (see dependencies) but they do not capture phase transitions or the scheduler's backpressure behavior under heterogenous sequence lengths.

Goal: produce minimal, high-signal anchors that reliably catch regressions introduced by kernel selection, attention optimization passes, and scheduling heuristics without causing CI noise. Anchors should be small in number, fast to run, and produce rich telemetry (KV cache hits, kernel switch counts, per-token time breakdown).
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic anchor corpus of 12 anchor shards that cover short/long prefix mixes, heavy KV reuse, and worst-case attention patterns is checked in to the bench repo.
Prefill-decoder harness components implemented: sequence-phase sampler, stage-aware traffic replay, and an automated kernel-exercise mode that forces kernel routing decisions for each run.

CI perf gate added to the mainline pipeline: compares median and 95th latency against the anchor baselines using bootstrap noise-modeling; gate fails only when effect size > defined threshold and signal-to-noise exceeds 2.0.

On failure, the CI output includes: representative spans, PR-links to the failing commit, a prioritized checklist of likely root causes (kernel change, scheduling config drift, quantization change), and a JIRA-style template with telemetry links for further investigation.
Documentation: design doc and runbook published in Confluence; README in bench repo explaining how to add/remove anchors and how to interpret CI artifacts.
tasks: Design anchor shard taxonomy and tagging scheme (by phase mix, KV-reuse, model size, batch shape)
Implement deterministic sequence-phase sampler library with seedable pseudo-randomness
Extend mixbench harness to expose per-token kernel route decisions and KV cache metrics
Add kernel-exercise mode which toggles kernel selection knobs to force alternate paths
Build noise-modeling utility to compute confidence intervals for quantile-based thresholds
Integrate CI perf gate job with artifacts upload (traces, kernel-switch logs, perf diffs)
Create Confluence runbook and bench repo README; include troubleshooting checklist
Run alpha anchor sweep against canary runtime on dedicated infra and collect baselines
progress_updates: 2026-03-10 - Asha Patel: Kickoff meeting with Runtime and KR teams. Agreed scope and anchor taxonomy draft. Decided to limit anchors to 12 shards for maintainability.
2026-03-11 - Liam O'Connor: POC sequence-phase sampler implemented. Deterministic seeding validated across CPU/GPU runs; reproduces same phase boundaries in 99/100 trials.
2026-03-12 - Mei Chen (KR): Kernel-exercise mode design reviewed. Mei recommended adding a kernel-routing override rather than patching the router, to minimize runtime drift.
2026-03-12 - Asha Patel: Noise-modeling prototype shows current CI variance would cause 30% false-positive rate; we will adopt bootstrap with effect-size thresholds to reduce noise.

2026-03-13 - Liam O'Connor: Integrated per-token kernel logs into bench artifacts. First anchor sweep against internal canary shows a 7% median regression after recent attention-fusion change — flagged for triage.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: use a small set of high-signal anchors (12) rather than a wide corpus to keep CI runtime < 30 minutes. Tradeoff: risk of missing rare path regressions but improves developer feedback cycle.

Decision: deterministic seeding + fixed hardware profile for anchors to maximize reproducibility. Tradeoff: may underrepresent multi-hardware interference seen in production; will complement with periodic large-scale stochastic runs.
Tradeoff: kernel-exercise mode may exercise unrealistic routes; we will label those runs separately in dashboards to avoid conflating with normal traffic.
Decision: CI gate will fail only on combined median+95th regression with effect-size threshold and required signal-to-noise ratio, to reduce flakiness.
review_feedback: 2026-03-12 - Mei Chen (KR): Requested inclusion of kernel-switch counters and per-layer attention time breakdown in artifact schema.
2026-03-13 - Priya Rao (SRE): Asked for a fallback policy in the CI job so that transient infra OOMs do not incorrectly mark perf regressions; added retry+skip logic with annotation.
2026-03-13 - Jonah Weiss (PM): Suggested adding one customer-derived anchor that mirrors a heavy conversational workload used by a key early adopter. Agreed to include as optional anchor.
risks: CI flakiness due to infra variability — mitigated by noise-modeling and hardware pins
Anchors becoming stale as models/profiles evolve — mitigate with quarterly anchor review and automated drift detector
Excessive maintenance overhead if anchors proliferate — mitigated via strict PR review checklist for adding anchors
